title: Machine learning links gut microbial modules with inflammatory and clinical features of major depression
summary: A single-center cross-sectional study of 102 inpatients with major depression and 38 controls used machine-learning feature selection on gut-microbiome profiles to identify nine biologically annotated microbial modules. Random forest with recursive feature elimination selected genera, and module scores were associated with inflammation and symptom dimensions. Functional pathways were inferred from 16S data rather than directly measured, and the associations do not establish causality or clinical utility. The small cohort and in-sample symptom associations require independent replication.
ai_technology: Random forest with recursive feature elimination; PLS-based multivariate modeling
organization: Sichuan Provincial People’s Hospital; University of Electronic Science and Technology of China; Deakin University

evidence.tested: Cross-sectional comparison of 102 MDD inpatients and 38 matched controls; feature selection and train/test evaluation of microbial profiles and clinical phenome measures; random forest/PLS-based biomarker discovery.
evidence.unknown: No independent external replication established; inferred functional potential is not measured microbial activity, and cross-sectional associations cannot establish causal effects or clinical benefit.
evidence.ai_role: Random forest with recursive feature elimination selected a parsimonious genus set within training data; PLS-based modeling linked microbial profiles to clinical and inflammatory measures.

source_review.scope: Publisher article-in-press PDF: abstract, introduction, full analysis strategy, participant and sample methods, AI/ML pipeline, and results including module/phenome associations.
